plugins.name: bee
plugins.description: Bee — a spec-driven TDD workflow navigator for AI-assisted development. Guides developers through the right level of process: triage, spec, architecture, TDD planning, execution, verification, and review.

skills.name: ai-ergonomics
skills.description: This skill should be used when evaluating how well code supports LLM-assisted development. Contains context window friendliness, explicitness, module boundaries, test-as-spec, and naming criteria.
skills.description_zh: 评估代码对 LLM 辅助开发的友好程度，检查上下文窗口适配、表达明确性、模块边界、测试作为规范及命名质量。

skills.name: ai-workflow
skills.description: This skill should be used when explaining why Bee follows spec-first TDD workflows, or when teaching mode is on. Contains the reasoning behind spec → plan → test → code ordering.
headings: Why Vertical Slicing Improves AI Focus
skills.description_zh: 解释 Bee 采用规范优先 TDD 工作流程的原因，或用于教学模式，说明规范、计划、测试、代码的顺序及其依据。

skills.name: architecture-patterns
skills.description: This skill should be used when evaluating architecture options, checking dependency direction, or deciding between onion, MVC, and simple patterns. Contains YAGNI-based decision criteria.
skills.description_zh: 评估架构方案和依赖方向，依据 YAGNI 原则在洋葱架构、MVC 与简单模式之间做选择。

skills.name: bee-state
skills.description: This skill should be used when updating workflow state in bee-state.local.md. Contains the full command reference for update-bee-state.sh including init, set, get, clear, all flags, and multi-line field syntax.
skills.description_zh: 更新 bee-state.local.md 工作流程状态，参考 update-bee-state.sh 的初始化、设置、读取、清除、参数和多行字段语法。

skills.name: boundary-generation
skills.description: This skill should be used after discovery completes on a greenfield project when the discovery document contains a Module Structure section. Contains the full procedure for parsing module boundaries, generating BOUNDARIES.md, and optionally linking it from CLAUDE.md.
skills.description_zh: 在新项目探索完成且探索文档包含模块结构后，解析模块边界、生成 BOUNDARIES.md，并可在 CLAUDE.md 中添加链接。

skills.name: brainstorming
skills.description: This skill should be used when the user wants to brainstorm, explore ideas, think through options, says 'let's brainstorm', 'what are our options', 'how might we', 'what if we', 'help me think through', 'explore approaches', or presents an open-ended problem without a clear solution. Covers cross-domain thinking where changing one dimension (product, tech, UX) can simplify another.
skills.description_zh: 针对开放问题开展头脑风暴，探索思路、选项和假设；通过跨产品、技术与体验维度思考，寻找能同时简化其他维度的方案。

skills.name: browser-testing
skills.description: This skill should be used when running browser-based verification. Supports two providers: Claude-in-Chrome (primary) and chrome-devtools-mcp (fallback). Contains tool reference, dev server detection, screenshot conventions, and graceful degradation.
skills.description_zh: 进行浏览器验证，优先使用 Claude-in-Chrome，备用 chrome-devtools-mcp；涵盖工具用法、开发服务器识别、截图约定和不可用时的降级处理。

skills.name: clean-code
skills.description: This skill should be used when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code. Contains SRP, DRY, YAGNI, naming, error handling, dependency direction, and Kent Beck's four rules of simple design.
headings: YAGNI — You Aren't Gonna Need It
Kent Beck's Four Rules of Simple Design
skills.description_zh: 在编写、评审或重构代码时应用单一职责、DRY、YAGNI、命名、错误处理、依赖方向及 Kent Beck 的简单设计四原则。

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: This skill should be used when performing code reviews, analyzing git hotspots, or detecting coupling. Contains Adam Tornhill's code-as-crime-scene methodology and effort sizing.
headings: Efferent Coupling (Who do I depend on?)
skills.description_zh: 开展代码评审、分析 Git 热点或发现耦合，采用 Adam Tornhill 的代码现场调查方法并估算工作量。

skills.name: collaboration-loop
skills.description: This skill should be used when processing @bee annotations in documents or managing [ ] Reviewed gates. Contains the exact comment card format and review loop rules. Load before handling any @bee comment.
skills.description_zh: 处理文档中的 @bee 注释或管理 Reviewed 审核关卡，依据规定的评论卡格式和评审循环执行协作。

skills.name: debugging
skills.description: This skill should be used when diagnosing failures, fixing bugs, or investigating why tests don't pass. Contains systematic debugging: reproduce first, read before you change, assume nothing, find root cause.
headings: Trial and Error is Last Resort
skills.description_zh: 诊断失败、修复缺陷或调查测试不通过的原因，采用先复现、修改前阅读、核实假设和寻找根因的系统调试流程。

skills.name: design-fundamentals
skills.description: This skill should be used when making UI/UX decisions, designing layouts, choosing colors and typography, writing UI specs, or reviewing visual components. Contains the two-path design flow (existing system vs greenfield discovery), accessibility rules, typography pairing, color palette guidance using Sanzo Wada's Dictionary of Color Combinations, spatial composition, anti-generic rules, and visual quality checklist.
skills.description_zh: 进行 UI/UX 决策、布局、颜色、字体、界面规范或组件评审，按已有设计系统或新项目探索两条路径处理，并检查可访问性、字体搭配、配色、空间组织与视觉质量。

skills.name: grill-me-with-context
skills.description: Interview the user about a plan or design with full codebase context. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking against the actual codebase, says 'grill me with context', 'challenge this against the code', 'does this plan fit our architecture', or presents a plan for a specific codebase and wants it pressure-tested against what actually exists. Differs from plain grill-me by grounding every question in the project's real architecture, patterns, and constraints.
headings: One question at a time — always via AskUserQuestion
When you find a gap — offer to brainstorm
skills.description_zh: 结合真实代码库采访并审查用户的计划或设计，将每个问题落到项目实际架构、模式和约束上，检验方案是否适合现有系统。

skills.name: grill-me
skills.description: Interview the user relentlessly about a plan, design, or idea until reaching shared understanding. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, asks to be grilled, says 'poke holes in this', 'challenge my design', 'what am I missing', or presents a plan and wants it pressure-tested before committing to it.
headings: One question at a time — always via AskUserQuestion
When you find a gap — offer to brainstorm
skills.description_zh: 围绕计划、设计或想法持续提问，查找漏洞和遗漏，直到双方形成共同理解，适用于实施前的压力审查。

skills.name: lsp-analysis
skills.description: This skill should be used when performing precise dependency analysis with LSP tools. Contains availability checking, graph reasoning, and graceful degradation.
skills.description_zh: 通过 LSP 工具进行精确依赖分析，先核对工具可用性，再推理依赖图，并在工具不可用时采用降级方案。

skills.name: model-tiers
skills.description: This skill should be used when an orchestrator needs to choose or resolve a model for a delegated agent — i.e. by /bee:planner when authoring a plan (assigning a capability tier per agent per slice) and by /bee:plan-implementer when executing one (resolving a tier to a concrete subagent model value). Contains the single source of truth mapping capability tiers (best / excellent / fast) to Claude Code subagent model values, with per-tier guidance for picking the right one. Load this skill instead of hardcoding any model name.
headings: Model tiers — the single source of truth
skills.description_zh: 为 Bee 规划器或实施编排器选择被委派代理的能力档位，并将档位映射到 Claude Code 子代理模型；依据统一映射与各档位指导，避免硬编码模型名称。

skills.name: requirement-architect
skills.description: Rewrites software requirements to lead to better code design and architecture. Use this skill whenever a user shares requirements, user stories, feature specs, acceptance criteria, or PRDs and wants them improved before development begins. Also trigger when a user says 'review my requirements', 'improve this spec', 'make this requirement better', 'rewrite this for better design', 'architecture-aware requirements', or asks how to write requirements that produce cleaner code. Trigger even when users paste requirements without explicitly asking for review — if the requirements contain design-limiting patterns (conditional chains, implementation details, ambiguous boundaries), proactively suggest improvements.
skills.description_zh: 在开发前改进软件需求、用户故事、功能规范、验收标准或 PRD，使其更利于代码设计和架构；识别条件链、过多实现细节和边界含糊等限制设计的表述。

skills.name: resolve-m-conflicts
skills.description: This skill should be used when resolving git merge conflicts. Parses conflict markers, shows clean side-by-side diffs, explains why each conflict occurred using git history, and presents resolution options via AskUserQuestion with reasoning for the recommended choice. Use this skill whenever the user mentions merge conflicts, says 'resolve conflicts', 'fix conflicts', or when git status shows unmerged paths.
headings: Step 3: Build Context — Why Did This Conflict Happen?
Step 4: Present Resolution Options via AskUserQuestion
How to decide the recommended option
skills.description_zh: 解决 Git 合并冲突，解析冲突标记、并排展示双方差异，结合历史解释成因，并给出解决选项及推荐理由供用户选择。

skills.name: spec-writing
skills.description: This skill should be used when writing specs, acceptance criteria, or slicing features into vertical slices. Contains adaptive depth by risk and out-of-scope capture.
skills.description_zh: 编写规范与验收标准，或将功能拆分为纵向切片；依据风险调整细节深度，并记录范围外事项。

skills.name: tdd-practices
skills.description: This skill should be used when writing a TDD plan, reviewing test quality, choosing between unit and integration tests, or applying red-green-refactor. Contains outside-in double-loop, test isolation, and test naming.
skills.description_zh: 制定 TDD 计划、评审测试质量、选择单元或集成测试以及执行红绿重构，涵盖由外向内的双循环、测试隔离与命名。

skills.name: try-it-yourself
skills.description: This skill should be used after all slices are verified and before review. Contains templates for generating contextual 'Try it yourself' manual verification steps based on what was built (frontend, backend, CLI, greenfield, library).
skills.description_zh: 在所有功能切片验证后、正式评审前，根据已构建的前端、后端、CLI、新项目或库，生成贴合上下文的手动试用验证步骤。

commands.name: architect
commands.description: Architectural health assessment grounded in domain language. Compares how a product describes itself against how the code is structured.
headings: Step 2: Spawn All 4 Agents in Parallel
Step 3: Merge Findings into Assessment Report
Step 5: Save Report and Collaboration Loop

commands.name: brainstorm
commands.description: Start a brainstorming session. Open-ended, collaborative idea generation for product, architecture, UX, or any problem space. Researches online, builds on your ideas, and helps narrow to the best path forward.

commands.name: browser-test
commands.description: Run browser-based regression tests against specs. Verifies acceptance criteria in a running app via Chrome MCP, produces pass/fail reports with screenshots. Read-only — does not modify code.
headings: Step 3: Dev Server Detection and Confirmation

commands.name: coach
commands.description: Analyze your development sessions and get actionable coaching insights

commands.name: discover
commands.description: Start a discovery session. A PM persona that interviews you (or synthesizes from transcripts) and produces a client-shareable PRD. Use standalone or let /bee invoke it automatically.

commands.name: help
commands.description: Explain Bee's features interactively — what each command does, when to use it, what artifacts it produces. Adapts to your project context.

commands.name: migrate
commands.description: Analyze a legacy and new codebase to produce a prioritized, independently-shippable migration plan.

commands.name: onboard
commands.description: Interactive developer onboarding for existing projects. Analyzes the codebase and delivers an adaptive walkthrough with knowledge checks.

commands.name: ping-pong
commands.description: Run ping-pong TDD on a spec. Two agents alternate — one writes a failing test, the other makes it pass — until all acceptance criteria are implemented.

commands.name: plan-implementer
commands.description: Canonical plan executor. Implements an execution plan one merged build agent per slice (tests + code together, at each slice's plan-assigned model tier), then reviews and verifies once at the end. Use when the user runs /bee:plan-implementer, says "implement the plan", "build the plan", "run the plan", or has been handed off from /bee:planner. Reads a plan at docs/plans/<feature>-plan.md.
headings: Step 1: Locate the plan and its artifacts
Step 2: Implement (one spawn per slice, at the plan's per-slice tier)
Step 3: Review at the end (single pass, once)

commands.name: planner
commands.description: Authors the execution plan — the prescriptive "how" that lets a lower-tier model write good code. Runs on the best model, once per feature. Given a spec, a ticket, or a prompt, it gathers code context (context-gatherer), then writes a per-slice plan carrying design structure (classes, method signatures, collaborators, control-flow outline), test strategy (new file vs modify existing), standards to honor (bee's craft skills), a single build-agent tier per slice, and per-slice quality checks. Applies hard-floor marks and persists to docs/plans/. Use when the user runs /bee:planner, says "plan this", "make a plan", "plan the spec/ticket", or has been routed here by /bee:spec-writer or /bee:start. Hands off to /bee:plan-implementer.
headings: Step 1: Locate and classify the input
Step 3: Ground in the craft skills
Step 5: Hard floors (final step of authoring)

commands.name: qc
commands.description: Quality coverage analysis with hotspot-driven test planning. Finds high-risk untested code and produces a prioritized test plan.
headings: Step 2: Spawn 3 Review Agents in Parallel
Step 4: PR Mode Execution (only when PR-id provided)

commands.name: review
commands.description: Standalone code review with hotspot analysis, tech debt prioritization, and developer coaching.
headings: Step 2: Spawn All 7 Agents in Parallel

commands.name: sdd
commands.description: Use spec to drive development. Works with or without a pre-built spec. With a spec path, skips to context → architecture → slice loop. Without a spec (or with a task description), runs the full workflow including triage → discovery → spec → architecture → code → test → verify → review.

commands.name: spec-writer
commands.description: Spec authoring link of Bee's plan-driven chain. Produces a testable, slice-decomposed spec from a discovery doc, a focused conversation, or a task description — via bee's spec-builder agent, which interviews the developer and writes docs/specs/[feature]-spec.md. Use when the user runs /bee:spec-writer, says "write a spec", "draft the requirements", "turn discovery into a spec", "spec out this feature", or has been routed here by /bee:start. Hands off to /bee:planner (which authors the execution plan, then hands to /bee:plan-implementer).

commands.name: start
commands.description: Triage router and the first command to run when the user doesn't know which Bee command applies. Takes a description, classifies the work (bug / small feature / large feature / exploratory / existing artifact pointer), detects high-risk context, and recommends the right chain entry — brainstorm, discover, spec-writer, planner, plan-implementer, or skip Bee entirely. Use when the user runs /bee:start, says "kick off a feature", "I want to build X", "we need to fix Y", "where do I start", or describes work without picking a command themselves.
headings: Step 5: Targeted elicitation (only if heuristic is unsure)
Step 1: Symlink Bee into Cursor’s config
Step 2: Add the Bee rule in Cursor
If you move or clone the Bee repo

description: Bee — a spec-driven TDD workflow navigator for AI-assisted development. Guides developers through the right level of process: triage, spec, architecture, TDD planning, execution, verification, and review.
